newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Jewish group wants hunt for accounts of Nazi elite.
newsitem.headline: Jewish group wants hunt for accounts of Nazi elite.

text.p: A Jewish group hunting for the unclaimed assets of Jews killed by Hitler said on Monday the real search should be for the Nazi elite's bank accounts because the assets of Holocaust victims were "peanuts" by comparison.

The U.S.-based rights group Simon Wiesenthal Centre said it had sent a list of 334 names of leading figures of the Third Reich to countries accused of Nazi ties and urged Swiss banks to reveal if their vaults contained any of the money.

"Victims' accounts are peanuts compared to the perpetrators' accounts," its founder Rabbi Marvin Hier told a news conference ahead of a two-day conference in Geneva on gold, art and other property looted by Nazi Germany, starting on Tuesday.
"Tremendous amounts of funds were transferred from the Third Reich. Almost half a century later, nobody has ever investigated such a list. That's the key to the entire mystery."
Listed individuals with the right to open foreign accounts ranged from Adolf Hitler to Nazi wives, mistresses and helpers.
But it is uncertain what, if any, Nazi riches can be traced nearly 50 years after the end of World War Two.
Hier claimed Swiss banks never looked for these funds. But Swiss authorites froze all German accounts during the war and turned any funds held by senior Nazis over to the Allies.
As the controversy grows, it is still unclear where the missing millions of Holocaust victims have gone.
Jewish groups charge Swiss banks hold billions of dollars in Jewish assets. But a search has yielded just $32 million and banking authorities say larger amounts are unlikely to be found.
Amid boycott threats from Jewish groups, Swiss businesses have launched a 265 million Swiss franc ($184 million) fund.
And the government plans a seven billion franc ($5 billion) humanitarian foundation to aid victims of the Holocaust and of other abuses by selling part of central bank gold reserves.
Hier called these Swiss efforts a "bold move" but added: "We shouldn't give them the Noble Prize for philantrophy."
His comments are unlikely to help at a time of growing domestic opposition to government efforts at compensation.

Many Swiss have been outraged by a scathing U.S. government report in May which alleged their country was a huge teller window for the Nazis, taking their plunder and the deposits of Jews on the run as well as gold from the teeth of those killed.
On Monday, the United States got blasted in a full-page advertisement in French-launguage daily Tribune de Geneve.
Put by Swiss environment activist, Franz Weber, it said the United States -- "a ruthless, shameless, blackmailing giant" -- was out to cause the downfall of the Swiss financial centre.

"The very nation which denied sanctuary to tens of thousands of desperate Jews during World War Two is pointing an accusing and moralising finger at Switzerland...instead of facing up to her own guilt- and crime-laden history," it said.
"A nation that not so long ago wiped out American Indians and enslaved millions of Black Africans, which dropped atomic bombs on innocent populations of Hiroshima and Nagasaki..."

"We need to see the real motive behind their proceedings -- it is none other than greed for power and money. Switzerland may have shortcomings but one thing is certain: Switzerland is not worse than the United States -- and not worse than Israel."
